issues.detail: The Greek 'διακονιαν' (diakonian) is a noun meaning 'ministry/service', not 'chức vụ' (office/position). The Vietnamese translation interprets it as 'if it is an office,' whereas the Greek implies 'whether [it is] ministry...'

The Greek 'ειτε' (eite) functions as 'whether' or 'either', creating a correlative structure. The Vietnamese uses 'Nếu là' (If it is), which changes the logical structure from a description of roles/types to a conditional statement.
